propositions: The project requires a comprehensive audit of documentation, source comments, and embedded prose against a defined standard baseline to establish evidence for future remediation.
Documentation and comments must conform to specific punctuation, diction, voice, and structure rules including prohibition of dashes, semicolons, contractions, and filler language.
A three-shard taxonomy allocates review responsibility across durable records and internal documentation, external documentation and shipped help, and developer comments and embedded prose.

Exploration agents must inventory all maintained surfaces in scope, apply precedence rules to avoid overlapping review, and deliver structured reports organized by shard before filtering and challenge passes.
Filtering agents must validate every consolidated proposal against evidence quality, factual accuracy, taxonomy placement, duplication, and prose conformance before final adjudication.

The audit produces a filtered proposal document citing repository paths, symbols, and implementation evidence with remediation actions and destinations, with no project file changes authorized at handoff.
